panels.name: The vintage blue rusted pickup truck driving
panels.summary: The vintage blue rusted pickup truck driving into the humid Mississippi Delta at dusk.
panels.caption: He headed south into the Mississippi Delta and worked bar to bar looking for the old man.
panels.prompt: Extreme wide shot, cinematic landscape. An old, beat-up 1970s blue rusted pickup truck (weathered light blue paint, oxidized rust patina, white cab roof) driving down a lonely two-lane asphalt road into the deep Mississippi Delta at dusk. Murky cypress swamps line both sides of the road, ancient cypress trees with hanging grey Spanish moss, humid mist drifting over dark bayou waters. Muted purple, deep green, and amber sunset sky. Style: Highly detailed modern graphic novel panel, crisp clean ink linework with fine cross-hatching, rich digital texture, muted but high-contrast cinematic lighting, clean cel and gradient shading, no messy watercolor wash, no blur. Include a torn paper caption box at the top with the exact text: "He headed south into the Mississippi Delta and worked bar to bar looking for the old man.". Use a messy handwritten marker font.

panels.prompt: Over-the-shoulder shot inside a dark, rustic wooden Delta juke joint. Only two people present in the room: a tall young adult man standing in the foreground, and the bartender behind the bar. In the foreground, standing tall on his feet at the wooden bar counter (not sitting, tall 6-foot-1 broad-shouldered 24-year-old adult man with long limbs, towering over the bar, athletic back, tousled dark brown hair, wearing a faded blue denim trucker jacket with a battered black guitar case slung across his broad back). From behind his tall shoulder, he holds out a crumpled sheet of paper with a rough charcoal pencil sketch of an elderly African-American man in a fedora. Across the scarred wooden bar counter, an uneasy African-American bartender in a stained apron looks at the paper sketch with nervous, guarded eyes, shaking his head and raising a hand dismissively to push the drawing away. The old bluesman is NOT physically present in the room. On the weathered wooden porch of a rustic Mississippi juke joint, a gruff African-American bouncer's hand firmly slams a heavy wooden door shut right in the young man's face, refusing to answer questions. Standing outside in the driving rain is the tall 6-foot-1, 24-year-old young adult man (broad shoulders, dark tousled wet hair, stubble, wearing a soaked faded denim trucker jacket with his battered black guitar case slung across his back), looking weary, frustrated, and shut out. Down the dark, rain-soaked road in the foggy background, distant flickering neon beer signs of other closed and unwelcoming bars fade into the misty night, showing a long week of rejection and dead ends. panels.caption: Midnight came. He drove to the crossroad, killed his headlights, stepped out, and waited to be found.
panels.prompt: Extreme wide shot, cinematic exterior at midnight. A realistic, dark rural intersection in the flat Mississippi Delta where a two-lane dark asphalt highway crosses an unpaved gravel country road at an organic, natural angle. Realistic natural road perspective, no symmetrical roads, no artificial geometry, no glowing sci-fi lines. Tall cypress trees draped with Spanish moss and weathered wooden telephone poles line the roadside, with creeping white ground fog rolling across the dark road and grassy ditch under a vast ink-black night sky with faint stars. Off to the side on the dark gravel shoulder, the vintage 1970s blue rusted pickup truck sits parked with its headlights completely turned off. In the center of the dark road intersection, the tall 6-foot-1, lean 24-year-old Kid stands solitary and motionless, holding his battered sunburst acoustic guitar by his side, waiting silently in the cold midnight fog to be found.
